title: Will Kevin Warsh say Credit at his Oct 2026 press conference?
rules: If the Chair of the Federal Reserve says Credit at his Oct 2026 post-FOMC meeting introductory remarks and Q+A, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
How this is resolved
Video of the Oct 2026 post-FOMC meeting introductory remarks and Q+A. 
If a consensus by Kalshi employees cannot be reached using video, internal & external (official) transcripts of the Oct 2026 post-FOMC meeting introductory remarks and Q+A will be used. 

Payout criteria: Exact phrase/word, or a plural or possessive form of the phrase/word.

Doesn't count for payout: Grammatical/tense inflections.

blind.reasoning: Warsh has held post-FOMC press conferences as chair (June, September 2026), but he hinted at holding fewer and gave a record-short one in September, so October's could be skipped or very brief. If it happens, 'credit' is a common Fed word (credit conditions, spreads, private credit, balance-sheet credit allocation), but shorter sessions cut the chances. Combining about 80-85% for a presser with about 60-65% for the word gives about 50%.
blind.falsifier: Warsh announces no press conference after the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting (resolves NO), or he says 'credit' in his opening remarks or answers (resolves YES).

final.reasoning: The market's 0.55 is only a few points above my estimate, and traders may know the presser schedule and Warsh's word frequency better than my limited research did. That edge is too small to justify a bet, so I pass.
